newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB's Gehrig says Swiss CPI may be overstated.
newsitem.headline: SNB's Gehrig says Swiss CPI may be overstated.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) board member Bruno Gehrig said on Monday the Swiss consumer price index (CPI) may be subject to some distortions, which could mean the figure was overstating domestic inflation.
"I think there are certain distortions," Gehrig said in a question and answer session following a speech here.
"For that reason perhaps our inflation goal should not be one percent but two percent," he said.
But Gehrig added that it would take more courage than he possessed to adopt a less restrictive inflation goal, especially given that the extent of the possible distortion was not yet known.
The SNB currently seeks to keep money growth on track with a medium term inflation goal of one percent per annum over five years.
But Gehrig said that before any changes could even be considered the Swiss Federal Statistics Office would first have to establish whether such distortions actually existed and how great they were.
Gehrig also stressed that on a long term basis tolerating a higher inflation rate would not produce lasting growth.
Speaking to Reuters after his speech Gehrig said that if such distortions did exist they were likely to be smaller than similar distortions which had been seen in the U.S. consumer price index.
